sections.title: How to Use This Manual
sections.html:
• Warm up: Gentle movement through the ranges used in the planned stretches.
  • Consent & communication: set a comfort target of 2–3 out of 10. Stop for sharp pain, numbness, tingling, or dizziness.
  • Dose: Static holds 20–30 seconds for 2–4 rounds per area. PNF contract 5 seconds, relax 15–20 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds.
  • Partner script: “Tell me if anything feels sharp or pinchy. I will stabilize one area and move slowly on your exhale.”
  • Core cues for every stretch: breathe slow, keep pelvis level, stabilize before moving the limb, never force end range.

Red flags to defer or modify: acute tear, recent surgery with restrictions, nerve symptoms down the leg, unstable pain flare.

sections.title: Legend
sections.html:
Methods: Assisted = partner moves or supports the limb, Strap = partner-guided with strap, Block = supported with yoga block, Bench = supported with bench or table, PNF = contract-relax technique.

Acronyms & Abbreviations:

  • ASIS = Anterior Superior Iliac Spine
  • PPT = Posterior Pelvic Tilt
  • PNF = Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation
  • IR = Internal Rotation
  • ER = External Rotation
  • IT band = Iliotibial Band
  • OA = Osteoarthritis
  • ACL = Anterior Cruciate Ligament
  • PCL = Posterior Cruciate Ligament
  • TKA = Total Knee Arthroplasty (knee replacement)
  • SLR = Straight-Leg Raise

sections.title: Partner Safety & Quick Screen
sections.html:
• Ask before each area: any recent injuries, surgeries, or nerve symptoms.
  • Observe: pelvic position, rib flare, facial tension, breath holding. Adjust range if any of these appear.
  • Stop and alert the instructor if: sharp joint pain, radiating symptoms, new swelling, or loss of motor control.

sections.title: Hamstrings
sections.html:
Targets

Hamstrings (biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus)

Quick Screen

  • Recent hamstring strain or posterior thigh bruising.
  • Lumbar radicular symptoms down the leg.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Supine SLR, Assisted

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes distal thigh just above knee, other at heel or forefoot. Strap optional for control.

Setup & Cues: knee extended, ankle neutral or slight dorsiflexion, pelvis heavy and square, exhale into end range.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

  1. Supine 90/90 Hamstring, Assisted (hip ~90°, extend knee)

Variations: slight IR or ER of femur to bias medial or lateral hamstrings.

Watch-outs: posterior pelvic tuck to fake range. Fix with firm pelvic hand and cue “keep belt line heavy.”

Props

Strap, small bolster under opposite knee.

Seated Forward Fold, Assisted

Photographed setup: Seated with legs extended and hands reaching forward along the legs.

Use the instructor-demonstrated seated position and explain any back contact before assisting. The participant controls the forward reach; do not push them farther into the fold.

This additional option accompanies the class demonstration. Use the instructor-approved duration and method. It is not automatically required.

sections.title: Adductor
sections.html:
Targets

Adductors (longus, brevis, magnus, gracilis, pectineus)

Quick Screen

  • Acute groin strain or adductor tendinopathy flare.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Supine Assisted Hip Abduction

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes ASIS, other at distal tibia or ankle to guide abduction with knee extended.

Cues: toes to ceiling, knee long, pelvis level, move on exhale.

Props

Yoga blocks, light strap for guided control.

Seated Butterfly, Assisted

Photographed setup: Seated on the table with knees bent outward and the feet together.

Show the seated position and explain the contact area before assisting. Use the instructor-demonstrated support and participant-controlled range. Do not press the knees down.

This additional option accompanies the class demonstration. Use the instructor-approved duration and method. It is not automatically required.

Supine Butterfly Variations, Assisted

Class variation: The participant is supine with hips and knees bent and the legs positioned outward. The two photographs show different practitioner support and hand placements.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Glute/Piriformis
sections.html:
Targets

Gluteus maximus, gluteus medius, piriformis

Quick Screen

  • Sciatic-type symptoms or anterior hip pinch.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Supine Figure-4, Assisted

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes opposite ASIS, other guides bent knee toward chest or opposite shoulder.

Cues: sacrum heavy, shin parallel, shoulders relaxed, breathe into back pocket.

  1. Supine Cross-Body Glute/Piriformis, Assisted

Regression: shorter lever, guide near knee. Progression: gentle ER bias at end range, do not force.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: lumbar rotation. Fix with opposite hip stabilization.

Props

Block under knee for passive support between reps.

Supported Figure-four Variation, Assisted

Class variation: Use the instructor-demonstrated figure-four variation shown in this view, with the bent leg supported by the practitioner.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Abductors / IT Band
sections.html:
Targets

Tensor fasciae latae (TFL), lateral hip tissues, IT band region

Quick Screen

  • Irritable greater trochanteric pain or acute lateral hip pain.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Supine Assisted Adduction Across Midline (TFL bias)

Hand Placement: one hand cups lateral ASIS to prevent hike, other guides leg across midline with slight hip flexion and IR.

Cues: ribs down, pelvis square, reach long through heel.

Props

Towel roll under waist, strap for gentle control.

Supine Hip Abductor Stretch, Assisted

Class variation: These alternate hip-abductor views show the participant supine, the leg supported and a stabilizing hand at the pelvis. Follow this demonstrated variation rather than assuming the side-lying top-leg-drop setup.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Calves
sections.html:
Targets

Gastrocnemius, soleus

Quick Screen

  • Acute Achilles tendinopathy or recent calf tear.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Supine Assisted Dorsiflexion, Knee Extended (gastroc bias)

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes tibia below knee, other cups ball of foot for dorsiflexion.

Cues: heel heavy, toes relaxed, motion at ankle not through knee hyperextension.

  1. Supine Assisted Dorsiflexion, Knee Flexed 20–30° (soleus bias)

Progression: subtle inversion or eversion sweeps to explore fibers.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: foot collapsing into supination or pronation. Support midfoot and cue neutral subtalar position.

Props

Strap, small towel under Achilles for comfort.

sections.title: Hip Flexors
sections.html:
Targets

Iliopsoas, rectus femoris

Quick Screen

  • Painful lumbar extension, spondylolisthesis, or anterior hip pinch.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Thomas Position Hip Flexor, Assisted (edge of table)

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes opposite ASIS, other on distal femur of hanging leg to guide extension with gentle PPT cue.

Cues: glute on, ribs down, do not arch low back, exhale as thigh lowers.

  1. Bench Assisted Short-Lever Hip Flexor

Support: partner controls lower-leg angle, gradually brings hip into extension while pelvis stays neutral. Add tiny PPT, then release.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: lumbar extension dump. Fix with rib-down cue and strong pelvic hand.

Props

Pad under knee, small lumbar pillow if needed.

sections.title: Quadriceps
sections.html:
Targets

Quadriceps (rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius)

Quick Screen

  • Anterior knee pain, recent ACL or PCL reconstruction, early post TKA.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Side-lying Assisted Quad

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes pelvis at iliac crest, other controls ankle or strap to flex knee. Slight hip extension biases rectus femoris.

Cues: knees parallel, hips stacked, press front hip forward gently, exhale as heel approaches glute.

  1. Prone Assisted Quad (pillow under abdomen)

Regression: shorter lever, hold at shin. Progression: small hip extension while maintaining neutral pelvis.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: anterior pelvic tilt. Fix with abdominal support and pelvic hand.

Props

Strap for ankle, bolster under knee if needed.

Images & Video

Caption: Assisted quadriceps stretch variations with pelvis stabilization and controlled hip extension.

Prone Table-edge Quadriceps, Assisted

Photographed setup: Participant face down near the table edge, one leg supported toward the floor and the other knee bent with practitioner support.

Have the instructor demonstrate the exact table-edge setup and supports before practice. Confirm the participant is stable before contact. Support the bent leg as demonstrated; do not copy the position without instructor guidance.

This additional option accompanies the class demonstration. Use the instructor-approved duration and method. It is not automatically required.

sections.title: How to Use This Manual
sections.html:
• Warm up: 3–5 minutes of gentle mobility before assisted stretching.
  • Consent and communication: agree on a comfort target of 2–3 out of 10. Stop for sharp pain, numbness, tingling, dizziness, or visual changes.
  • Dose: Static holds 20–30 seconds for 2–4 rounds per area. PNF contract 5 seconds, relax 15–20 seconds, repeat 2–3 rounds.
  • Partner script: “Tell me immediately if anything feels sharp or numb. I will stabilize one area and move slowly on your exhale.”
  • Core cues: breathe slow, ribs stacked over pelvis, scapula controlled, never force end range.

Red flags to defer or modify:

  • Recent shoulder dislocation or fracture, recent surgery without clearance.
  • Nerve symptoms into hand, unexplained night pain, acute inflammatory flare.

sections.title: Pecs, Anterior Shoulder
sections.html:
Targets

  • Pectoralis major (clavicular and sternal fibers)
  • Pectoralis minor
  • Anterior shoulder line

Quick Screen

  • Anterior shoulder pain or instability
  • Recent GH dislocation, post-op precautions

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Pec Major (abducted 60–90°) - seated OR supine

    • Hand placement: stabilize anterior shoulder and scapula, support forearm near wrist to guide horizontal abduction.
    • Cues: ribs down, scapula glides, no anterior humeral glide, exhale as chest opens.
    • Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

      • Setup: posteriorly tilt and depress scapula, guide slight horizontal abduction with minimal GH rotation.

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • Do not force end range, avoid anterior glide. If pinch, reduce abduction angle and increase scapular posterior tilt control.

Props

  • Half foam roller along cervical and thoracic spine

Seated Pec / Chest Stretch

Class variation: The participant sits on the table with the arms positioned behind the torso. Use the demonstrated arm support and contact points for this chest-stretch variation.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

Approved variations: The instructor-demonstrated seated chest-opener is included here as a variation rather than a separate tracker entry. Use the approved seated setup and practitioner support, and confirm participant agreement before assisting.

sections.title: Posterior Shoulder and Capsule
sections.html:
Targets

  • Posterior RTC
  • Posterior GH capsule
  • Posterior deltoid

Quick Screen

  • Sharp posterior shoulder pain
  • Recent labral repair precautions, instability

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Cross-Body Adduction

    • Hand placement: stabilize scapula against rib cage, guide humerus across body at shoulder height.
    • Cues: scapula stays flat, ribs down, exhale as arm comes across.
    • Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF: “gently push your arm outward into my hand” 5 seconds, relax 15–20 seconds.

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • If anterior shoulder pinch, reduce IR and ensure scapular stabilization. Keep movement smooth and within comfort.

sections.title: Shoulder ER Bias
sections.html:
Targets

  • GH external rotation range
  • Anterior capsule tolerance
  • Subscapularis length

Quick Screen

  • Anterior instability, history of anterior dislocation
  • Painful end-range ER

Primary Assisted Options

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • Avoid anterior humeral glide. If pinch at front, reduce abduction angle and increase scapular control.

Shoulder External Rotation, Assisted

Class variation: The supine participant’s bent arm is supported during the instructor-demonstrated external-rotation application. Use the demonstrated angle; this photograph does not establish a precise abduction measurement.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

Approved variations: Use the arm angle demonstrated by your instructor. The 30–45° abduction setup, when assigned, is a variation of this technique rather than a separate tracker entry. The photograph does not establish a precise angle.

sections.title: Shoulder IR and Lats
sections.html:
Targets

  • GH internal rotation
  • Posterior cuff balance
  • Latissimus dorsi and teres major length

Quick Screen

  • Posterior shoulder pain that feels sharp
  • Recent RC repair, painful overhead impingement

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Overhead Lat Bias

    • Setup: stabilize lower ribs and guide humerus into flexion with slight ER, keep scapula upwardly rotating without rib flare.

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • If shoulder pinch, reduce overhead angle, add more scapular upward rotation and posterior tilt control.

Props

  • Small towel roll under humerus or elbow for support

Shoulder Internal Rotation, Assisted

Class variation: The participant is supine with the bent arm supported. These two views show the instructor-identified internal-rotation application and its hand placement; use the demonstrated angle.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

Approved variations: Use the arm angle demonstrated by your instructor. The 30–45° abduction setup, when assigned, is a variation of this technique rather than a separate tracker entry. Keep the elbow supported as demonstrated.

sections.title: Biceps
sections.html:
Targets

  • Biceps brachii, long and short head
  • Brachialis bias with elbow position

Quick Screen

  • Anterior elbow pain
  • Distal biceps repair precautions, nerve symptoms in forearm

Primary Assisted Options

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • Avoid anterior shoulder glide. If elbow pain, reduce extension angle and try neutral or pronated forearm.

Biceps Stretch, Assisted

Class variation: The participant sits with the arm reaching behind the torso and the practitioner supporting the arm. Use the hand and forearm orientation demonstrated in class rather than inferring a grip bias from the photograph.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

Approved variations: Use the instructor-approved palm-up (supinated) or neutral-grip version with the demonstrated hand and forearm support. These grip variations share one competency entry. Record the variation in a practice note if useful; do not infer a grip bias from the photograph.

sections.title: Triceps
sections.html:
Targets

  • Triceps brachii long head with overhead position
  • Posterior elbow line

Quick Screen

  • Posterior elbow pain
  • Recent elbow surgery, shoulder impingement with overhead positions

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Overhead Triceps

    • Hand placement: stabilize lower ribs and scapula, support wrist or forearm to guide elbow flexion overhead.
    • Cues: ribs stacked, neck long, gentle overhead angle, exhale into range.
    • Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF: “gently try to straighten the elbow into my hand” 5 seconds, relax 15–20 seconds.

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • If shoulder pinch, lower the overhead angle and increase scapular upward rotation and posterior tilt control.

sections.title: Forearm and Wrist
sections.html:
Targets

  • Forearm flexor, pronator group
  • Forearm extensor, supinator group
  • Wrist capsule comfort range

Quick Screen

  • Recent wrist or elbow surgery
  • Nerve symptoms in hand, acute medial or lateral epicondylalgia flare

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Wrist and Forearm Flexor Bias

    • Hand placement: stabilize distal forearm, extend wrist and fingers with gentle elbow extension and slight supination.
    • Cues: fingers relaxed, stretch in forearm not elbow joint, breathe slow.
    • Dose: 15–25 seconds × 2–3. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

      • Setup: flex wrist and fingers with elbow extension and slight pronation to bias common extensors.

Watch-outs and Fixes

  • Avoid nerve tension signs. Stop for tingling or altered sensation and notify the instructor before continuing.

Props

  • Towel roll under wrist or forearm for comfort and leverage

sections.title: Cervical (Neck)
sections.html:
Targets

C-spine flexors/extensors, lateral flexors, rotators

Quick Screen

  • Recent concussion or whiplash, dizziness, visual changes, numbness or tingling into arm.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Cervical Lateral Flexion

Hand Placement: one hand anchors at opposite upper shoulder, other hand cradles head at parietal area. Avoid pressure on jaw.

Cues: shoulders relaxed, small range, chin slightly tucked, breathe slow.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–3 per side. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

  1. Assisted Cervical Rotation

Setup: partner supports base of skull and opposite shoulder, rotates head slowly to comfortable end range.

Watch-outs: no end-range springing, stop for dizziness or visual changes.

Props

Small towel under neck for comfort.

Partner Cues

  • “Let the shoulder melt down.”
  • “Tiny chin tuck, breathe into your nose.”
  • “You control the range, tell me if you want less.”

Gentle Supported Neck Stretch

Class variation: The photograph shows the practitioner supporting the head near the table edge. This is the instructor-demonstrated gentle supported neck stretch. The still image does not establish the movement or support needed. Review the exact support, technique and course boundaries with the instructor before practice. Do not infer a pulling force from the image.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Upper Trap & Levator
sections.html:
Targets

UT and LS with selective head position

Quick Screen

  • Neck pain with radiating symptoms, dizziness, recent C-spine injury.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Upper Trapezius Stretch

Hand Placement: one hand depresses shoulder girdle, other hand guides head into contralateral lateral flexion.

Cues: ribs down, do not shrug, gentle nose breathing.

  1. Assisted Levator Scapulae Stretch

Setup: turn head about 45° away, then flex and gently tuck chin toward armpit while depressing shoulder.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–3. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: do not torque the neck, avoid jaw pressure, stop for tingling.

Partner Cues

  • “Keep the shoulder heavy, let me do the work.”
  • “Exhale as I ease the angle.”

sections.title: Thoracic Rotation
sections.html:
Targets

T-spine rotators, posterior shoulder capsule comfort range

Quick Screen

  • Rib pain, acute shoulder pain, dizziness with head turning.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Side-lying Thoracic Open Book

Setup: use the instructor-demonstrated side-lying setup and supports. The partner guides the arm and trunk through the approved rotation while supporting the participant.

Dose: 20–30 seconds × 2–4. PNF is assessed separately using the approved lower-body application in Start Here.

Watch-outs: lumbar substitution; keep pelvis anchored.

Partner Cues

  • “Keep pelvis quiet, breathe into back ribs.”
  • “Let the shoulder blade slide as you exhale.”

Supported Thoracic Rotation, Lab Variation

Class variation: The participant is side-lying with practitioner contact at the trunk and pelvis. Both photographs show this thoracic-rotation application; the wider view is presented first to show the overall setup.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Lats & Side Body
sections.html:
Targets

Latissimus dorsi, lateral trunk fascia, intercostals

Quick Screen

  • Shoulder impingement symptoms, rib pain, recent shoulder surgery.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Overhead Side Reach

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes lower ribs, other hand guides arm overhead while side-bending trunk away.

Cues: ribs stacked, shoulder blade glides, length through fingertips.

Partner Cues

  • “Keep ribs stacked over pelvis.”
  • “Reach long, not hard.”

sections.title: Side-lying QL
sections.html:
Targets

QL, obliques, lateral fascial line

Quick Screen

  • Sharp low back pain, radiating symptoms into leg, recent lumbar injury.

Primary Assisted Options

  1. Assisted Side-lying QL Lengthening

Hand Placement: one hand stabilizes iliac crest, other hand guides rib cage into gentle caudal-cranial separation.

Cues: keep pelvis level, long through waist, breathe into side ribs.

Partner Cues

  • “Lengthen the waist, not the low back.”
  • “Breathe into the side ribs.”

sections.title: Lumbar Rotation
sections.html:
Supine Lumbar Rotation, Assisted

Class variation: The participant is supine with one bent leg positioned across the body and practitioner contact at the leg and opposite upper torso. This is the instructor-identified lumbar-rotation application. Follow the demonstrated setup and supports; do not use the thoracic-rotation cues as a substitute.

Use the exact setup, supports and hand placement demonstrated by the instructor. Explain the contact areas and obtain agreement before assisting. The participant may pause or stop at any time.

Follow the instructor-approved movement and duration. This photographed option is not automatically a required competency.

sections.title: Operation and approved application
sections.html:
Use only Theragun and Theragun Pro Plus units used in our lab. Confirm the exact model and attachment with your instructor before practice.

  1. Explain the activity and obtain agreement. Review the manufacturer precautions for the exact device and defer any concern to the instructor.
  2. With the device off, check condition, charge, and secure the approved attachment. Keep hands, hair and clothing away from moving parts.
  3. Use the instructor-approved setting and application over the agreed soft-tissue area. Check comfort throughout; stop for pain, altered sensation, dizziness or another unexpected response.
  4. Power off before changing attachments. Follow the approved equipment cleaning procedure before the next user.

Pro Plus offers multiple attachments and functions. Use only the mode demonstrated and approved for this lab; the presence of an attachment does not make it a required skill.

Therabody: model-specific user manuals · Manufacturer precautions

sections.title: Safety and instructor boundaries
sections.html:
Manufacturer precautions differ by device and mode. Do not apply percussion directly to the head, face, throat, neck, genital area, wounds or areas your instructor has excluded. Recent injury or surgery, altered sensation, vascular or bleeding conditions, implanted devices and other concerns require instructor review and the appropriate professional advice before use.

This is a course checkpoint, not a substitute for the complete device-specific warnings.

Read the full manufacturer precautions
